## Native submission seam and replay semantics

Pinned `DefaultChunkRenderer.render(ChunkRenderMatrices, CommandList,
ChunkRenderListIterable, TerrainRenderPass, CameraTransform)` calls native
`ShaderChunkRenderer.begin` once, sets projection/model-view matrices, iterates
regions and performs this sequence:

1. `fillCommandBuffer(batch, region, storage, renderList, camera, renderPass,
   useBlockFaceCulling)` at bytecode133.
2. Ensure shared index-buffer capacity and prepare the current region tessellation.
3. `setModelMatrixUniforms(shader, region, camera)` at201.
4. `executeDrawBatch(commandList, tessellation, batch)` at211.

The loop owns one mutable `MultiDrawBatch`; filling the next region overwrites
its arrays. Keeping its pointer is not keeping a region submission. Actual
`GLRenderDevice$ImmediateDrawCommandList.multiDrawElementsBaseVertex` reads
count/index-pointer/base-vertex arrays and immediately invokes
`GL32C.nglMultiDrawElementsBaseVertex(IJIJIJ)V` at37. The existing timing hooks
already cover these seams; another profiler is unnecessary.

A duplicate at that GL call primes **only the current region**, then shades that
region. It can remove hidden work within that region; later regions have not yet
contributed depth. It is not whole-pass priming. Sodium already has distance
ordering; this source work does not measure remaining overdraw.

Whole-pass priming would require a bounded per-current-pass snapshot of each
region's copied count/index-pointer/base-vertex arrays, tessellation and region
offset, then replay in native order. Snapshotting the submission during the
first traversal while issuing its coverage draw could avoid a second visibility
traversal, upload or sprite/task update. Colour draws would subsequently replay
those submissions. This is an unimplemented design boundary, not a current
capability or an excuse to cache cross-frame visibility. Re-running
`SodiumWorldRenderer.drawChunkLayer` or a renderer's whole `render` method would
repeat setup/assembly/state and does not satisfy the assigned same-submission
contract.

Native SOLID and CUTOUT map to Iris `Pass.TERRAIN` and
`Pass.TERRAIN_CUTOUT`. Sodium's vanilla solid entry invokes solid then cutout;
translucent maps separately. Shadows map to shadow variants and must remain
excluded. A full priming stage per terrain pass must preserve solid-colour then
cutout-colour order and LEQUAL equality winners; no EQUAL shortcut is admitted.

## Exact vertex/program and uniform boundary

Pinned `SodiumPrograms.createShader(IrisRenderingPipeline, Pass, ProgramSource,
AlphaTest, CustomUniforms, Supplier<ImmutableSet<Integer>>,
Map<PatchShaderType, GlShader>)` receives the **actual already transformed and
compiled** native stage objects. It attaches them to a builder, invokes private
`buildProgram`, then deletes their handles on normal and exceptional return.
A second builder before native deletion is the concrete possible seam for
sharing the same native vertex object. Recompiling a vertex-source copy is a
weaker contract and is not proposed.

Native `buildProgram` binds the exact attributes: position0, colour1, texCoord2,
light/data3, normal10, mc_Entity11, midUV12, tangent13 and midBlock14. Its
interface factory creates the ordinary Iris `SodiumShader` with the same pass,
pipeline, source directives, custom uniforms, flip-state supplier and alpha
test. A future coverage program must retain this vertex ABI, native matrices,
region offset, draw translations, texCoord shrink and current frame/deformation/
TAA inputs. Its fragment shader would need the sibling's admitted exact coverage
ABI, not an assumed `texture(...).a` substitute.

Sharing a vertex object does **not establish** cross-program link invariance.
The native source contains no `invariant gl_Position`; its position includes
waving, iron-bar depth bias and native jitter. The inspected native Sodium/Common
transformer outputs contain no invariant injection string. Actual transformed
native/coverage output and Apple driver behaviour were not checked. A different
fragment link can change live outputs/optimisation, so exact depth equality
cannot be asserted from object sharing alone. No invariant declaration was
added to native source to bypass this boundary.

`SodiumShader.setupState` applies blend overrides, updates common/custom uniforms,
images and samplers, binds atlas/lightmap and sets shrink. Native
`resetState` clears active uniforms/samplers, restores blend override and binds
Minecraft's main target. Calling that reset between coverage and colour would
therefore change FBO ownership; it is not a harmless program unbind. A future
implementation must use native program-specific input population and recover the
original terrain FBO/program/texture state explicitly.

## Coverage STOP and GL acceptance boundary

Native terrain samples the selected atlas at201–207 and discards alpha<=.5
at210–212 subject to its POM condition. However
`terrainIPBR.glsl` has an additional snow-layer discard at2654 under
`GBUFFERS_TERRAIN && TAA`, independent of `SNOWY_WORLD`. The sibling's active
native398 preprocessing confirms RP_MODE1/IPBR/TAA and material interval
10952<=mat<10956. This worker independently extracted the exact original member
and confirmed its branch. An alpha-only prepass would write depth for fragments
that native shading discards; native geometry behind those holes could then be
rejected. That is a concrete coverage counterexample and prevents this bounded
renderer stage from being released. No snow/PBR/TAA/preset option was disabled.

Even with admitted coverage, runtime gates would remain: exact native atlas
filter/sampler/shrink and alpha-test transformation; no POM/gl_FragDepth/scene-
depth-read/side-effect path; no DH; depth-test enabled, native depth-mask true and
LEQUAL; exact existing scene-depth attachment; blend-disabled opaque MRT writes
for all active targets. Native terrain writes atlas alpha to target0 and1 to
auxiliary targets; passing atlas alpha>.5 is not proof of opaque blend semantics.
The native properties do not expressly disable terrain blending; actual state
has not been inspected.

The temporary draw must write no colour and must restore every indexed MRT colour
mask, depth mask/function, draw/read FBO, current program, active texture/sampler
bindings, viewport/scissor and blend state before native colour. Native state-
cache coherence also matters: raw GL temporary edits cannot leave Mojang/Iris
cached values inconsistent. No `early_fragment_tests` declaration is permitted
to make depth writes survive discard. No target/history/cadence addition is
needed or staged.

No bootstrap mixin/config is supplied because source admission failed. A default-
false development gate would only be useful after coverage/program equality and
state admission; it cannot make unsafe draws safe. Parent may close this bounded
stage from the source counterexample without a build or client run. The broad B9
mechanism, other packs and project Goal remain unfinished; this report does not
claim a runtime failure, global impossibility or project completion.

been accepted as adapter quality or a performance/support result.

## Three serial native quality runs

Root uses the existing compiled, verified dev harness, with no measurement or
benchmark mode. These exact commands physically exclude the main mod through

GPU timing off. Never run the three windows concurrently. If source dev classes
need a build, root performs it before any client and rechecks artifact identity;

## Conditional source and graph certificate

1. In all three dimension wrappers, composite3 includes the same pinned program.
   With `WORLD_BLUR=0`, the preprocessed fragment main is exactly a level-zero
   integer texel fetch of colortex0 RGB and `vec4(color, 1.0)` output to target 0.
   Its vertex shader is the fullscreen `ftransform()` path. Depth, DH/Voxy blur,
   bloom fog and its own mip request are all inside the positive-blur branch.
   There is no composite3 compute companion in the pinned archives.
2. `pipelineSettings.glsl` requests R11F_G11F_B10F for target 0 and
   `colortex0Clear=true`. The format line is inside a block comment used for
   shader directives; **actual Iris parsing and driver storage must be observed**.
   This RGB format has no stored alpha. Both paths should sample alpha 1;
   writing alpha 1 is not evidence of a generic RGBA identity. The exact
   InternalTextureFormat bytecode maps this name to GL format 35898 and RGB.
   Conversion of subnormal/exceptional RGB, NaNs, infinities, or changed GL state
   is not proved identical by a string declaration or the Python tests.
3. Native bloom fog is applied in composite1 when blur is zero, and composite3
   when blur is positive. The End explicitly undefines bloom fog. Bloom disabled
   also undefines it. Tests preserve those actual dimension gates; removing the
   zero-blur pass must not remove the earlier bloom-fog operation.
4. In exact Iris, PropertiesPreprocessor consumes effective string options and
   environment defines. StandardMacros emits IRIS_VERSION as 10812. ShaderPack
   evaluates enabled properties into its disabled-program list; its source
   loader returns null for those program paths. CompositeRenderer skips an
   invalid graphics source before constructing its framebuffer or executing its
   automatic output flips. This is graph deletion, not a skipped draw with a
   stale flip. With no compute companion it adds no replacement compute pass.
5. A pass snapshots BufferFlipper state. IrisSamplers selects alternate storage
   for a flipped target and main storage otherwise; RenderTargets constructs
   the output framebuffer from the opposite storage. Constructor output flips
   then affect later snapshots. Runtime mip generation uses that pass's selected
   input storage. Native composite1 already writes/flips target 0 in all
   dimensions; removing composite3 does not introduce the first-use custom
   sampler case. No explicit flip/scale override exists in the pinned properties.

Let P be the physical target holding logical color C after composite1; Q is its
other storage. These are symbolic identities, not observed GL object IDs.

| Step, native motion blur off | Original | Elided candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| composite3 | P(C) → Q(C), flip current to Q | Absent; current stays P(C) |
| composite4 input/mips | Regenerate mips from Q(C) | Regenerate mips from P(C) |
| composite4 output | Native target 3 bloom result | Same logical target 3 result if C and GL state are equal |
| composite5 | Reads current Q(C), writes target 3 | Reads current P(C), writes target 3 |
| composite6/TAA | Reads target 3, writes 3 and history 2 | Same logical inputs and history requirement |
| final and next frame | Native target 3/final path; target 0 cleared | Same path; target 0 cleared |

The archives have no dimension composite2 wrapper; its reserved program source
is not an intervening producer. The earlier deferred1 pass **also requests
target-0 mipmaps**. Composite4's unconditional regeneration overwrites the
current image's earlier mip chain. With native motion blur enabled, composite4
additionally writes target 0 and flips it after that mip generation. Earlier
physical mip/filter state could then differ for composite5. R1 deliberately
keeps motion-blur-enabled paths native pending a separate certificate; this is
an unresolved state question, not an observed pixel failure.

Exact FinalPassRenderer `lambda$new$1` returns before creating a swap-copy for
targets in the clear list. With the observed clear directive correctly parsed,
target 0 should therefore not gain a compensating final copy when its parity
changes. Actual swap lists and calls remain runtime evidence requirements.

ClearPassCreator constructs clears for **both physical storages** of cleared
targets. RenderTargets requests a full clear on construction and resize; the
pipeline chooses full/regular clears accordingly. FinalPassRenderer resets
minification filtering on both target storages after rendering. These bytecode
paths support initialized first-frame and next-frame operation. They do not
prove that every actual reload, dimension transition, target resize or failed
reload followed those paths. Persistent history lives in other targets and
must remain synchronized; target 0's cleared status alone does not prove TAA
history equality.

## Algorithm, selection and saved work

With native `WATER_REFLECT_QUALITY=2`, terrain direct lighting invokes the
finite-area GGX correction despite that option's water name. R2 replaces
only this correction for fully eligible distant/minified rough SOLID terrain.
For unit normal N, light L and view-toward-eye V, the zero-radius limit is

`NoH² = clamp((NoL + NoV)² / (2 + 2 VoL), 0, 1)`.

It uses the same normal/view/light inputs and same positive NoL as upstream.
For NoL=1, NoV=0.5 and VoL=0.5 the result is 0.75. The native low-quality
reflected-direction expression instead gives 0.25, and is not reused.
R2 preserves the upstream roughness transform, GGX D, Fresnel F, normal/light
prefactor, saturation/compression and downstream highlight/shadow/moon weights.
This **does not assert equal integrated highlight energy**: finite area and
point area produce different contributions and require quality evidence.

The fully coarse branch returns before `GetNoHSquared`; it avoids its
finite-disc tangent/bitangent/Newton arithmetic and associated square roots,
divisions and dot-product expressions. It adds a point-limit denominator and
the eligibility/footprint calculations. Native weight 0 evaluates the native
correction alone. Transition weight between 0 and 1 evaluates both responses
and blends **compressed specular output contributions**. Thus transition
pixels incur extra work; all-pixel full-plus-cheap evaluation is avoided.
No texture query, shadow kernel, material classification, geometry, pass,
target, history, LUT or update cadence is removed or added. Native
terrainIPBR, smoothnessD/reflections, normals/RT4, masks, TAA, emission,
recolor, shadowMult/lightmap and SSS remain live and unchanged.

Selection requires normal core bridge 2, enabled 1 and preset 0–2; Quality
ordinal 3 returns native. Distances are `length(viewPos)` in Minecraft blocks.
The blend begins at `max(near, far - max(transition, 1 block))` and is fully
coarse at far. A configured zero transition receives a one-block minimum
continuous band. Core distances must satisfy their existing valid ranges.

Atlas texels per screen pixel are measured as
`max(length(dFdx(texCoord) * atlasSize), length(dFdy(texCoord) * atlasSize))`.
These derivatives execute at the **first fragment-main statement, before
texture sampling, discard and material divergence**. The footprint weight is
zero at ≤1 texel/pixel, blends from 1 to 2 and is full at ≥2. No derivative
query is introduced behind a material branch or sampling shortcut.

Only Overworld Iris `renderStage == MC_RENDER_STAGE_TERRAIN_SOLID` is eligible.
The pinned Iris enum maps SOLID to ordinal 8 and the macro/supplier use its
native phase; actual linked value and consuming draw remain unverified.
Cutout/foliage, emissive and SSS materials remain native. Native roughness
selection is full for smoothnessG ≤0.20, fades to native at 0.35; glossy
materials remain native. NoL/NoV must exceed 0.25, VoL must exceed −0.95,
vectors must be unit within squared-length tolerance 0.001, and nonfinite
or invalid inputs return native. `RoL=2 NoL NoV−VoL` fades the approximation
from 0.92 to 0.98, keeping disc/glint directions native. These guards avoid
singular half-vectors and grazing cases without changing upstream fallback
arithmetic.

Water/underwater, hand, non-terrain, non-Overworld, absent stage macro, DH,
Voxy, custom PBR, generated normals and Colorwheel return native. Unknown
archives/options/resources require parent-side original selection; the helper
does not certify all 398 options or pack identity itself. Changing such
inputs cannot be accepted from this prototype.

## Coordinates, jitter and history

No distance LOD bands are proposed. Side scale is dimensionless; coordinates
and velocity are explicitly in internal pixels, output pixels, or normalized
logical UV. Camera translations and view-space depth are Minecraft blocks.
Initial fixed design scale is .75 only after the new temporal algorithm earns
admission; no scale/filter/scene search. For output extent `O=(W,H)`, internal
extent `I=floor(.75*O)` and each resource allocation `A`, valid scene rectangle
is `[0,I)`. Only exact initially admitted dimensions are allowed.

Let `u=(outputPixel+.5)/O` be an **unjittered output UV**. Let `delta_t` be the
total current projection displacement in UV. A geometry point at unjittered
`u` is rasterized at `q=u+delta_t`. Current low-grid center `i` represents
unjittered sample `(i+.5)/I-delta_t`. Thus reconstruction's fractional current
key is `(u+delta_t)*I-.5`, physical keys are integers in the valid rectangle,
and physical current UV is `q*I/A`. This distinction avoids multiplying
full-output history UV by .75. Use `texelFetch` level0 for new current taps and
integer nearest metadata; do not infer derivatives inside validity branches.

Native `TAAJitter(coord,w)` adds `offset[framemod8]*amplitude*w/view`; since
clip NDC maps to UV through .5, native UV displacement is
`offset*amplitude/(2*view)`, not `offset/view`. Amplitude is .125/.33/1 for
selected TAA_JITTER=1/2/3. Native fragment inverse-jitter uses `w=-.5` with
screen UV in terrain/basic/water material paths. A new phase must update that
same helper contract consistently in vertex and fragment paths, including
water refractive position reconstruction. Do not patch vertices alone.

Small native jitter1 does not broadly distribute internal samples. Proposed
co-design adds a declared four-frame reconstruction phase of `(±.25,±.25)`
internal pixels, with native selected jitter superimposed in internal-pixel
units. Total clip displacement is `(2*phase+nativeOffset*amplitude)*w/I`;
total UV displacement is `(phase+.5*nativeOffset*amplitude)/I`. Four phases
cover a denser sample lattice; their ability to retain detail remains a
hypothesis. It changes temporal sample positions while preserving the user's
option values. It must not be described as identical native jitter or proven
AA preservation. TAA off or TAA_JITTER=0 means scale1, no added phase.

Reproject from the **selected current sample's unjittered UV and depth**, using
the native inverse/current/previous matrices and camera offset (taa:60–78).
This yields previous unjittered output UV because c2 would store an unjittered
output lattice. Do not add previous jitter again to full-output c2 sampling.
Current depth and material belong to the same selected internal sample;
do not inverse-project full-output UV using unrelated low-grid depth. Keep
native movement in output pixels `(u-prevUV)*O` and camera displacement in
blocks. Normalize expected previous view depth against the prior `far`, not
current internal/output pixel dimensions.

Proposed c2 alpha stores nonnegative normalized linear view depth
`(-viewPos.z)/far` for each output pixel; a negative sentinel marks no-history
entity/hand/invalid-current cases. Compare fetched **nearest** previous alpha
with expected previous-view depth reconstructed from current sample/world
position; never bilinearly blend validity depth across an edge. FP16 precision
needs conservative error bounds derived from quantization and local depth
spread, and a driver check. c7 previous depth is SSR-specific, half-resolution
and overwritten before c6; borrowing it would give the wrong history lifetime.

Reserve a small c2-only metadata strip, excluded from Catmull history support:
output size/scale code, algorithm marker, consecutive frame token, previous far,
and applicable reset/medium/projection state. Encode dimensions/frame tokens
in exact FP16-safe chunks; decode once in c6 vertex and flat-pass eligibility.
c3 visible output is never replaced by metadata. Near strip support, use fresh
current seed or clamped safe history support. Existing renderer epoch reset
must clear both physical c2 sides on scale/world/resize/reload transitions.
This extends existing shader state; no new observer, target, pass or Java
temporal framework is proposed. Exact strip packing/reset triggers must fit
before implementation admission; inability to carry a needed trigger closes
this design at that concrete boundary. Source Clear=false alone proves no
driver history retention/reset behavior.

A concrete upper bound fits **eight c2 texels /32 half-float components**, at
`(x=0..7,y=0)`. Decode only integer level0 fetches in c6 vertex; no fragment
metadata fetch loop. Native option map changes require the existing reload/reset
seam; the metadata is not an options-discovery system.

## Resolve and rejection behavior

In c6, form a small bounded current footprint around `(u+delta_t)*I-.5`.
Gather 3 × 3 level0 current colors and paired depth0/depth1/material keys once,
clamped to valid internal extent. Select a surface-consistent current estimate
and construct color/variance bounds from the matching surface samples. Reuse
these taps for depth spread and the native leaf edge handling. This replaces
the native full-output c3 neighborhood at taa:106–132; it does not run that
neighborhood on an already spatially reconstructed full-output current image.

Read full-output c2 with the **selected native** movement filter (native five
explicit level0 Catmull taps or native linear choice). Fetch nearest previous
depth separately. Reject history before blending for out-of-bounds reprojected
UV/support, invalid/NaN history, reset/nonconsecutive marker, depth/surface
mismatch, no-TAA masks, or unfit motion/projection/medium discontinuity. Existing
native masks 100–199 entities and 254 remain history-excluded; 253 retains
reduced-edge leaf treatment. Reduced-resolution current seed for these masks
may itself be visibly lossy and needs actual quality review, not an assertion.
Cloud obstruction/entity handling stays active with mapped c5 depth.

For accepted history, clamp in the current low-grid surface neighborhood,
then combine native smoothing/movement factors with reconstruction sample
confidence: a well-centered fresh sample has more current weight; farther
low-grid samples rely more on valid history. This confidence is algorithmic,
not a preset change. Do not increase history persistence across a disocclusion
to hide blur. Write the resolved color to visible c3 and c2 RGB and current
selected-surface depth to c2 alpha in the same pass. Depth rejects use current
seed immediately; there is no stale-history crossfade on a scale transition.

Native reprojection has no object motion vectors, previous material map or
matching previous transparent depth0. Adding one previous opaque depth does
not solve water/refraction/cloud animation, moving foliage or entity edges.
Reactive current depth0/depth1/material/cloud evidence can reduce history use;
it cannot manufacture native detail. These are high-risk admission scenes.
If required metadata or coordinate coverage cannot fit this bounded design,
report that blocker and stop; do not add a universal framework.

## Rejected alternative and filtering boundary

One tempting exact algebraic annihilator is `shadowTime == 0`: the sampled
shadow is multiplied by max(NdotLM*shadowTime,0) at339. With the native filtering
macro unchanged, the local subsurfaceHighlight is later multiplied by that zero
shadow too. However shadowTime is the fourth power of
`abs(sunVisibility - 0.5)*2` (terrain69–71 and equivalent callers). Exact zero
requires sunVisibility exactly0.5, corresponding to the sun at the horizon;
night is not zero. A threshold would change native transition/lighting. R11
day7000 offers no evidence of this exact predicate or useful coverage: actual
sunAngle/SdotU/shadowTime were not captured. Inactivity there is a daylight-scene
inference, not a measured uniform. This isolated-value branch does not meet the
substantial active-work gate and is not selected for implementation or a new

Native `deferred1.glsl` writes ordinary cloud-linear depth into c5 alpha and
preserves the VL factor at the singleton. Native `composite1.glsl` receives that
factor as a flat varying. `GetVolumetricLight` uses it for the whole screen

is retained outside the singleton when composite1 writes c5 again.

mix(invNoonFactor2 * .875 + .125, 1.0, max(vlSceneIntensity, rainFactor2))

ordinary cloud-depth alpha at 1, this term changes from .125 to 1, an **8× change
in this selected VL multiplier**. Other angle, distance, shadow, color and
saturation factors still apply; no final-image brightness ratio is claimed.
Reading ordinary cloud alpha also disconnects the adaptive feedback recurrence:
updates written at the singleton are not read back by the following vertices.

records.text:
# Complementary native shadow-family sequence R10

Preparation owner `shadow_sequence_r10`; parent owns launcher/tests, integration,
review and idle Mac GPU. **SOURCE READY / no real client, experiment clock or
runtime window opened.** Parent GO plus final review is required before execution.
R9 stays CLOSED PARTIAL:164/157 →217/229, no return/restoration or accepted gain.
R10 addresses its demonstrated model-mediated handoff failure using one persistent
serial invocation of the existing launcher. No shader/profiler changes or old
source, profile, world, capture, result or closed-window alteration.

## Frozen inputs and bounded acceptance

Three fresh APFS `cp -cR` clones of stopped
`run-workloads/effect-rate-work-area-r3/client`, created under existing runtime
lock plus source-world `session.lock`, reside at
`run-workloads/complementary-shadow-sequence-r10/{original,removal,return}/client`.
All238 source-world files were hashed before/after and matched in every clone;
`dev/logs/complementary-shadow-sequence-r10/source-world-before.json` preserves
individual SHA256s. Preparation released both locks and proved zero clients.
No old source/profile/world mutation. Initial clones have no owner/client/session.

Same untouched original ComplementaryReimagined_r5.9.3 ZIP SHA256
`fed6c879e732cf7fc7bc6570ebb1def43235aa7e96f62859fbdbdbfa0b484b38` in all arms.
Only supplied sidecar line: `SHADOW_QUALITY=2`, `SHADOW_QUALITY=-1`, `SHADOW_QUALITY=2`.
Expected actual398-option maps are copied from the independent
[native contract](COMPLEMENTARY_SHADOW_NATIVE_CONTRACT_R9.md); all other native
values including distance192/native AA remain identical. Source dependencies
jointly alter generation, receivers, Overworld shafts, time-angle, cloud occlusion,
underwater fog and fallback lighting. Discovered option booleans are not evaluated
path activity. This deliberately degraded diagnostic is not a product preset,
isolated generation timing or exact cost ceiling.

Matched scene: grassy wooded coast/slope x256.5/y95/z768.5,yaw135°/pitch9°,
clear/day7000, native fullscreen1920×1200, render12/simulation8, Vsyncfalse/cap260.
No DH, no selected file resource packs/PBR pack. Minecraft1.21.1/NeoForge21.1.253/
Java21/Iris1.8.12/Sodium0.6.13; expected AppleM3Max/OpenGL4.1 Metal91.7 from retained
R9 capture. Actual R10 receipt must match this scene/GPU. DH3.3.3 remains pinned
but excluded from these plans; Photonv1.3b remains pinned but is not tested here.
Exact runtime artifacts/source/classes/resources are in `freeze.json` full
`buildFingerprint`, validated against unchanged BSLR6 freeze SHA256
`36b7511a6040ba8aed95f47a2707839edea16bc555c2b7867f62a011318103b8`.
No build/download/encoder/Windows operation occurred.

Full pre-GO `freeze.py` checks source/build/archive/commands/profile/options/control
and complete source/clone world files. Its `freeze.json` pins30 input files,
including launcher and runner, plus full build fingerprint and actual scene
expectations. Parent must rerun this before GO if the owned launcher changes.
Plans retain four existing compilation/resource skips, observer/profiler/timing/
benchmark flags false, same named capture properties. Runner uses existing
`capture_when_ready` after actual readiness and existing absolute one-shot
birth/argv/profile exact-client stop. Parent’s launcher review is independent.

## Existing launcher sequence and stop procedure

Ignored runner `dev/logs/complementary-shadow-sequence-r10/runner.py` is102lines.
It receives one fixed aware-UTC overall end from parent GO, rejects insufficient
full-bracket margin before any arm, and gives each existing supervisor165seconds.
Require165seconds plus35seconds overall teardown margin before each launch.
Usual R9 startup was approximately18seconds; this allows the existing90-second
readout. Slower startup/missing readouts fails this bracket without tuning/retry.
The original12-minute overall proposal leaves serial launch/closure headroom;
actual authorized start/end must be recorded from GO, never from prep or R9.

`dc.supervise(session)` is synchronous. Each next arm follows authoritative
supervisor return, exact owned-process absence, zero clients/free lock, successful
explicit shader/in-world/fullscreen readiness, saved/decoded capture and automatic
stop with retained exact-client proof, actual native map/scene/focus and existing600/
1800 readout/capture receipt checks. No model turn between arms. Current launcher
internally performs its existing source/build guards; no new profiling framework.
After terminal client absence/free-lock, bundled Pillow12.3.0 `Image.load()` fully
decodes each screenshot, requires PNG1920×1200, recomputes receipt SHA256 and
restricts the resolved path to that private profile’s
`screenshots/<capture_when_ready>.png`. Invalid image/hash/path terminates before
next arm. This small acceptance check is outside the preceding quiet client.
Only one expected `runClientLodOff` failure block/task/exit143 with launcher
exit_code1 can qualify `BUILD FAILED`; additional build/task/non143 failures
are rejected even when143 is also present. Other shader/control errors fail. Missing receipt, refusal, timeout, occupied lane or
insufficient margin terminates sequence; no retry, broader kill or window reset.
A refused stop can leave the existing supervisor holding ownership: preserve it
and report exact proofs rather than forcing a process/group shutdown.

After parent review/GO, launch as ONE persistent exec handle:

```sh
/Users/pippo/.cache/codex-runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3 dev/logs/complementary-shadow-sequence-r10/runner.py --overall-end-utc '<parent fixed UTC end>'
```

Record tool session/PID/birth/full argv before quiet hold. `sequence.json` records
